title: Governor Braun announces new storm recovery texting service for Hoosiers affected by storms
text:
Governor Braun announces new storm recovery texting service for Hoosiers affected by storms
Governor Mike Braun announced on Aug. 26 a new texting tool designed to help Indiana residents impacted by recent severe storms and flooding access disaster recovery resources in their communities.
Through Indiana 211, residents can now text IN211HELP to 898-211 at any time. The service prompts users to select the type of assistance they need and provides a list of disaster-specific resources based on their zip code. "Hoosiers impacted by these storms are focused on taking care of their families, their homes and their communities, and they shouldn’t have to spend hours searching for the help they need," said Governor Braun. "This new Indiana 211 disaster resources texting service puts disaster resources directly in the hands of Hoosiers and makes it easier to connect with available assistance as Indiana continues its recovery."
Indiana 211 has played an important role in responding to recent storms by connecting affected residents with assistance and resources. The development of tools like the new disaster texting service aims to make it easier for those impacted by storms to identify and access needed support within their local area.
Residents who require additional help can call 2-1-1 or visit IN211.org, where they can search for community disaster resources, submit a Disaster Damage Reporting Form, apply for State Disaster Relief Funds or Military Family Relief Funds, and connect with the Indiana Department of Homeland Security’s Disaster Recovery Hub.
To use the Indiana 211 Disaster Texting Service, individuals should text IN211HELP to 898-211 and follow prompts that request a zip code and type of resource needed. The system then sends information about available local resources directly via text message based on selections made during the process. Standard messaging rates may apply; users can reply STOP to opt out or HELP for more information.
Braun contributed through roles on school boards, state representation, championed over 40 bills that became law during his Senate term, achieved growth of his company into a national entity employing thousands, graduated summa cum laude from Wabash College before earning an MBA from Harvard Business School, has been married for 49 years raising four children, won election to the U.S. Senate in 2018 before becoming governor—all according to the official website.
